Working notes — ticket routing

- Tested action: chose C (regional office) for all tickets. Only accepted: REQ-2401 and REQ-2409.
- Both accepted tickets were large shipment requests from the south region.
- C was rejected for all other tested cases: claim/east, invoice/north, refund/north, refund/east, shipment/north, and multiple invoice/north tickets.
- Rule indicated so far: use C/regional office only for shipment requests originating from the south region. Whether “large” is required or just correlated is unconfirmed.
- Do not route C for claims, invoices, refunds, or shipments from non-south regions.
- Subject phrases like “client asking twice,” “second attempt,” “no rush,” “scanned not typed,” and “same as last month” did not make C valid.
- Sender/source has not shown a clear effect; do not use it yet.
- No evidence yet for choosing A (standard queue) vs B (priority desk) when C is invalid. Need trials on non-south/non-shipment requests.
- Next: if shipment + south, try C. Otherwise test A/B to learn valid routing.

Working notes — ticket routing

- Confirmed accepted: C/regional office for large shipment requests from south (REQ-2401, 2409, 2410). B/priority desk accepted for large refund request from south (REQ-2415).
- New: B is not general for south/large: rejected for claim/south/large (2411). B also rejected for shipment/east/small (2419).
- A/standard queue still has no accepted case. A rejected for invoice/east/large (2412), refund/south/small (2413), invoice/south/small (2414), invoice/south/large (2416), claim/north/small (2417), shipment/east/small (2418).
- C rejected for non-shipment types (claim/east, invoice/north, refund/north, refund/east) and shipment/north. But for shipment/east/small, A and B were both rejected separately; therefore C is likely valid for shipment/east/small. Do not rule out C for non-south shipments; region rule is at least south+east for shipments.
- Size requirement for C/shipment is unconfirmed; east small may still be C. For B/refund, only large south tested; small south refund not yet tested with B.
- Subject phrases (“second attempt,” “client asking twice,” “no rush,” “scanned not typed,” “same as last month,” “regional office”) show no independent effect.
- Sender/source still no clear effect.
- Rule so far: valid option depends on request type + region; not one desk per request type. C is linked to shipments (south/east likely; not north). B is linked to some refunds (south). A unknown.
- Next: test C on shipment/east/small; test B on refund/south/small; test B/C on invoice/south (A rejected); test A/C on claim/south (B rejected); test A/B on claim/north, invoice/north, refund/north/east.
